jobAdDetails.description:
Join Sapiens as our Lead Business Value Delivery Architect / Lead Solution Architect and play a pivotal role in taking client-facing insurance solutions from the sales cycle through delivery and into SaaS and AI platform migration, holding every engagement to a designed business outcome rather than an evolving list of requirements.

This is a role that sits between presales and delivery and stays engaged across both, spanning P&C, Life, and in future Reinsurance, with a particular focus on the non functional and operational requirements our industry consistently under-invests in. If you are deeply fluent in insurance product suites and platform roadmaps, comfortable holding both a head of claims and an engineer in the same conversation, and driven to keep clients and internal teams honest to the outcomes they signed up for - we'd love to hear from you.
jobAdDetails.requirements:
You'll own the professional and content thread of the solution end to end – across four connected areas of impact:
 
Value Definition – Presales solution design
 
  • Engage during the sales cycle, from general discovery through down select, to build product and industry context on the opportunity.
  • Frame the solution around the client's business outcomes, not a requirements checklist. Map what they are trying to achieve to what the platform actually delivers.
  • Establish a business outcome baseline with the client: what they will be able to do post go live that they cannot do today, and how both sides will measure it.
  • Own the definition of done, agreed jointly with the client.
  • Explicitly cover non functional and operational requirements: performance, scale, availability, security, integration, data migration, operability, and support, rather than leaving them to surface in build.
  • Feed into the implementation plan: the right order of implementation and the known dependencies, especially those on the client.
  • Where the platform does not meet the client's expected outcomes, own the resolution with Product and R&D. Either secure a commitment to build it into the core platform, with timelines aligned accordingly, or design it into the extension layer shipped with the core. The SA owns these conversations.
  • Act as the next layer of depth behind the presales and industry expert team. Presales surfaces the opportunity, the SA architects the solution.
  • Support the bid with clearly stated assumptions. The fixed price commercial construct itself is owned by Sales and the PD.
 
Delivery integrity
 
  • Move into rapid planning immediately after signing. Harden the solution against what the platform delivers, steering toward standard configuration over bespoke build.
  • Hand over a clear, documented solution design to the delivery team at the start of build, and safeguard the integrity of that design through delivery.
  • Hold all parties, internal teams and the client, accountable to the agreed business outcomes and how they will be achieved. This is outcome and professional accountability. The PM or PD holds delivery and the client to scope, timeline, and commitments.
  • Stay engaged through quarterly business reviews to catch outcome or value drift early.
  • Apply the definition of done. The project is complete only when the client is positioned to realise the value agreed at the outset, not simply when the system goes live.
 
Migration
 
  • For assigned clients, own migration outcomes through the analyse, dispose, bridge, and migrate framework, across the existing product portfolio and beyond.
  • Define, with each client, the specific value the migration unlocks and the KPIs that will confirm it. Migration is a value conversation, not only a technical one.
 
Tooling, AI, and continuous improvement
 
  • Serve as the first internal customer for AI in delivery, and own the tools and the standard for how they are used.
  • Set which source wins when inputs conflict: signed document over email, email over deck, deck over verbal.
  • Set what a human must verify in AI drafted work, rather than approve on sight.
  • Flag what the inputs do not say: tacit process, stakeholder disagreement, edge cases, not just what the AI summarised.
  • Work as part of the SA group to improve processes, outputs, and tools for quicker, better implementations, especially the SaaS migration factory, including a feedback loop from delivery back to discovery to recalibrate where discovery got the scope wrong.
 
What Success Looks Like:
 
  • Every signed programme has a documented, client agreed business outcome baseline, a joint definition of done, and go live success criteria.
  • Non functional and operational requirements are surfaced and designed in up front, not discovered in build.
  • Platform gaps are resolved deliberately, through a core platform commitment or an extension layer build, rather than emerging during delivery.
  • Delivery builds to the handed over design with minimal rework driven by scope or requirements ambiguity.
  • The SA group's processes, tools, and outputs measurably shorten implementations over time.
jobAdDetails.responsibilities:
You have a strong track record of designing or leading solution design in complex, enterprise-scale P&C insurance implementations, ideally across both presales and delivery. Extensive, hands-on P&C experience is essential for this role.
  • Deep P&C domain expertise across policy administration, underwriting, billing and claims, covering personal, commercial and/or specialty lines. Exposure to Reinsurance or the London Market is a plus.
  • Able to speak credibly to both a Head of Claims or Underwriting and an engineer.
  • Strong on non-functional and operational requirements, not only functional design: performance, scale, availability, security, integration and operability.
  • Proven ability to keep internal teams and clients aligned to agreed business outcomes. This accountability is central to the role, so it is a required skill, not just a welcome personality trait.
  • Experience with, or strong aptitude for, migrating P&C legacy or core systems to SaaS, including policy and claims data conversion.
  • Comfortable working in a function that is still being built. Process and tooling will be defined alongside the first deals.
  • Ideally, hands-on experience with cloud-native platforms and a proven track record at Born-in-the-Cloud (BIC) companies, bringing modern SaaS delivery practices to a global enterprise environment.
  • Skilled at using AI-driven tools and platforms to design, optimise and scale enterprise solution architectures.

jobAdDetails.title: Vice President - QA
jobAdDetails.description:
Description
 
The VP, Quality Engineering, Delivery owns the vision, strategy, and execution of quality assurance across all Sapiens’ Property & Casualty (P&C) and Life delivery projects. The role spans the global organization of Quality Analysts, test automation, and performance Quality Analysts embedded in customer implementation, SaaS migration and SaaS support programs. The owner sets enterprise-wide quality standards and governance, and partners with delivery leadership to enhance quality, reduce production risk, and strengthen customer trust across insurance platforms. The role combines strategic quality leadership, organizational and budget ownership, technology and automation modernization, and AI-augmented quality engineering to scale a high-performing, accountable global QA function. 

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Define and own the global QA strategy, vision, and multi-year roadmap across manual testing, automation, and performance engineering for all delivery projects.
  • Build, lead, and scale a global, multi-site QA organization, including QA Managers, Automation Managers, Performance Engineering leads, and their teams.
  • Own the enterprise delivery quality governance framework, including standards, policies, metrics, KPIs, and executive-level reporting on quality status, risk, and release readiness across all products and releases.
  • Champion Agile, SAFE and iterative delivery practices across the QA organization, ensuring quality is embedded early and continuously across the SDLC.
  • Define and govern enterprise-wide adoption of AI-augmented quality engineering practices, including AI-assisted test generation, defect and failure analysis, predictive quality insights, and responsible-AI usage standards. 
  • Drive enterprise test automation and performance engineering strategy, including framework standardization, CI/CD-integrated quality gates, tool rationalization, and reusable engineering assets.
  • Build organizational capability through hiring, org design, career pathing, succession planning, and development of QA Managers and future quality leaders.
  • Drive continuous improvement in quality culture and practices, including shift-left testing, risk-based coverage, exploratory testing, and expert testing.

Must Have Skills & Qualifications 
Experience & Background 

  • 20+ years of progressive experience in software quality assurance or quality engineering, including 5+ years in a VP, Senior Director, or Head of QA capacity leading global, multi-disciplinary teams.
  • Proven experience leading scaled and skilled QA organizations, across manual testing, automation, and performance engineering functions across multiple geographies.
  • Strong track record of building and scaling AI usage in QA, and test automation programs (functional, API, performance).
  • Experience in insurance, financial services, healthcare or other complex, regulated enterprise software domains is strongly preferred.

Technical & Functional Skills
 
  • Strong understanding of test strategy and test coverage, aligned to business processes and system processes
  • Strong command of quality metrics, KPIs, risk-based testing methodologies, and quality governance frameworks appropriate for enterprise-scale delivery.
  • Deep, cross-disciplinary expertise across manual testing, test automation frameworks, performance engineering, and API/database validation practices.
  • Strong grasp of test management tools (e.g., Jira, Zephyr), and CI/CD-integrated test automation.
  • Strong knowledge of automation tooling and approaches (e.g., Selenium, Playwright, API testing tools, performance testing tools) and how AI/GenAI is applied to test generation, defect analysis, and self-healing automation.

Personal Attributes 

  • Demonstrated ability to lead, structure, and scale a large, geographically distributed organization.
  • Executive presence and the ability to engage confidently with C-level clients and internal leadership.
  • Change-oriented mindset with readiness to be hands-on when needed
  • Readiness to travel and support global stakeholders and teams across time zones as required.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication in English

Why Join Us:
 
  • Shape the global quality vision for a leading insurance technology company, with direct influence on customer trust, and business outcomes.
  • Lead and build a world-class, multi-disciplinary QA organization spanning manual testing, automation, and performance engineering across geographies.
  • Operate at the intersection of quality leadership, AI-augmented engineering, and modern SaaS delivery, with a mandate to modernize and scale enterprise quality practices.

jobAdDetails.title: Senior Agentic AI Engineer
jobAdDetails.description:
About the Role
Insurance software implementations are among the most complex, document-heavy, and process-intensive programmes in enterprise technology. A single implementation can involve thousands of configuration decisions, hundreds of requirement documents, and years of delivery time. Sapiens is rebuilding how that work gets done — using production-grade AI agents that operate across the full implementation lifecycle, from pre-sales and scoping through to configuration, testing, and go-live.
 
Work You'll Do
Agent architecture & orchestration
  • Design and implement agentic systems capable of multi-step reasoning, planning, tool use, and workflow execution against complex, document-intensive implementation processes
  • Build stateful workflows using LangGraph or equivalent — including branching, retries, self-correction, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and reusable orchestration patterns
  • Engineer for long-horizon reliability — multi-step task completion, recovery from compounding errors, planning under uncertainty, and robust tool use when individual steps fail
  • Build the reasoning behind high-stakes implementation decisions — criteria-grounded outputs, structured review patterns, and auditable rationales that delivery consultants can act on and defend
Retrieval, grounding & context engineering
  • Develop end-to-end RAG pipelines: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector and hybrid retrieval, reranking, contextual compression, and grounding strategies
  • Engineer memory and context management — conversational state, persistent memory, retrieval-aware context assembly, and token-efficient context selection
  • Apply MCP-style tool and context interfaces so agents access the right information at the right time across enterprise knowledge repositories, document sources, and structured configuration data
Reliability, evaluation & safety
  • Implement observability and tracing for prompts, tool calls, retrieval quality, agent traces, failures, drift, latency, and production behaviour
  • Apply guardrails, safety controls, and failure-handling to reduce hallucinations in agents whose outputs practitioners act on directly in live client settings
  • Evaluate agents at trajectory and task level — multi-step task success, failure-mode and regression analysis, sandboxed test environments — alongside retrieval and generation quality metrics, automated checks, and human review
Integration & production craft
  • Build integrations with internal and external tools, APIs, enterprise systems, databases, and model providers so agents operate reliably within real delivery workflows
  • Deliver production-quality Python code with strong practices in testing, CI/CD, logging, versioning, and documentation; make architecture decisions that balance quality, reliability, latency, cost, and model risk
  • Translate ambiguous, high-complexity implementation processes into robust system logic and reusable AI patterns; stay current with advances in agentic systems and translate research into practical engineering decisions
 
Required Qualifications
  • Demonstrated depth building and shipping production agentic AI systems — we weigh shipped systems over years in a title
  • Strong, hands-on experience with LangGraph or equivalent agentic orchestration frameworks, including custom orchestration
  • Deep proficiency in Python — clean, testable, production-ready code
  • Experience designing and optimising end-to-end RAG systems: indexing, retrieval, reranking, grounding, and evaluation
  • Daily working proficiency with Claude (Anthropic API) and Claude Code — you use these tools every day, not occasionally
  • Experience building and deploying agents on Azure AI Foundry or an equivalent enterprise cloud AI platform
  • Practical understanding of LLM behaviour — strengths, limitations, hallucination risks, reasoning constraints, and the evaluation methods used to measure them
  • Experience evaluating and debugging agent behaviour at trajectory and task level, not just output quality
  • Hands-on experience with MCP-based interoperability patterns and tool-calling agent design
  • Modern software practices: testing, CI/CD, observability, tracing, and debugging for LLM-based systems in production
 
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with multi-agent orchestration and agent collaboration patterns
  • Familiarity with vector databases — Pinecone, Weaviate, Azure AI Search, OpenSearch
  • Experience building agents that process complex, unstructured document types — contracts, RFPs, configuration files, regulatory documents
  • Exposure to model adaptation techniques such as LoRA or QLoRA
  • Prior work in insurance, financial services, or enterprise SaaS implementation environments
  • Demonstrated habit of staying current with AI research, benchmarks, and emerging engineering patterns

jobAdDetails.title: AI Solution Engineer
jobAdDetails.description:
About the Role:-

Sapiens is scaling AI across its Sapiens insurance platform and the teams that build, test, and implement it. We’re looking for an AI Solution Engineer to take our AI use cases from pilot to production - across automation, development, QA, and Implementation Engineering (IE). You’ll work hands-on with LLM-based agents, MCP tooling, and Claude/Anthropic APIs to design, build, and scale systems that materially reduce manual effort across our client implementation projects. This is not a research role - it’s a build-and-ship role. You’ll own AI initiatives end-to-end: from proof of concept to a tool that Dev engineers and QA teams use every day.

What You’ll Do:
  • Develop & scale AI-powered tools for defect analysis, test automation, and performance engineering — turning working prototypes into reliable, project-agnostic systems used across multiple client implementations.
  • Build and extend agentic workflows using Claude/Anthropic APIs, MCP servers, and orchestration patterns (e.g., Playwright-based agents, Jira/Confluence integrations, RAG pipelines etc).
  • Support the Dev team directly — build AI tooling into the development workflow itself: code-review assistance, code and unit-test generation, legacy-code comprehension, and adoption of coding agents across development squads.
  • Own the automation layer: design generic, reusable engines (not one-off scripts) — for example, extending browser automation frameworks into scalable, flows-based architectures.
  • Partner with QA and Implementation Engineering to identify high-volume, repeatable problems (bug triage, root-cause classification, test coverage gaps, defect-to-process mapping) and turn them into AI-driven pipelines.
  • Accelerate Implementation Engineering delivery — AI-assisted configuration and data-mapping validation, requirement-to-test traceability, and generation of implementation and handover documentation from project artifacts.
  • Productionize AI initiatives: take internal tools from Claude-based prototypes to hardened services (e.g., Azure AI Foundry, API-based orchestration), with proper data validation, gating, and reporting.
  • Build reporting & insight layers: structured system prompts, dashboards, and analytics that give leadership clear, quantified visibility into AI impact (hours saved, defect trends, coverage gaps).
  • Drive AI governance: help define and maintain tracking standards for how AI is used and measured across Bug, Bug Customer, and Test workflows etc.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with QA, Dev, Performance, and Implementation teams across multiple concurrent client projects.
 
What We’re Looking For:
  • 3+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, with real production code (not just notebooks/POCs).
  • At least 2 years, Practical experience building with LLM APIs (Anthropic/Claude, OpenAI, or similar) - prompt engineering, tool use/function calling, agentic pipelines, RAG.
  • Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol) or similar tool-orchestration frameworks is a strong plus.
  • Solid programming skills in Python and/or JavaScript/TypeScript (Node.js).
  • Experience with test automation frameworks (Playwright, Selenium, or similar) and CI/test infrastructure.
  • Experience building developer-facing tooling and working inside the SDLC (code review, version control workflows, CI/CD pipelines) — you understand how engineers work before you try to automate it.
  • Familiarity with Jira/Confluence and working with structured project data at scale – advantage
  • Comfort turning ambiguous business problems into scoped, shippable tools — you prototype fast, then productionize.
  • Strong communication skills; comfortable working directly with QA, engineering, and leadership stakeholders across multiple projects.

Nice to Have:
  • Background in the insurance industry (P&C, Core Systems, Policy/Claims/Billing) – advantage
  • Experience with Azure AI Foundry or other enterprise AI orchestration platforms.

Why Join Us:
  • Work at the centre of Sapiens’ AI transformation — not on the sidelines of it.
  • High ownership: your tools will be used across multiple live client      implementations from day one.
  • Direct collaboration with Dev engineers, QA, automation, and AI leadership.
 
About Sapiens :-
Sapiens International Corporation is a global leader in intelligent insurance software solutions. With Sapiens’ robust platform, customer-driven partnerships, and rich ecosystem, insurers are empowered to future-proof their organizations with operational excellence in a rapidly changing marketplace. We help insurers harness the power of AI and advanced automation to support core solutions for property and casualty, workers’ compensation, and life insurance, including reinsurance, financial & compliance, data & analytics, digital, and decision management. Sapiens boasts a longtime global presence, serving over 600 customers in more than 30 countries with its innovative SaaS offerings. Recognized by industry experts and selected for the Microsoft Top 100 Partner program, Sapiens is committed to partnering with our customers for their entire transformation journey and is continuously innovating to ensure their success. For More information visit us on www.sapiens.com.
 
Sapiens is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and strive to create an inclusive work environment that embraces individuals from diverse backgrounds.

jobAdDetails.title: Director Delivery Devops
jobAdDetails.description:
Description

The Director, Delivery DevOps owns the delivery DevOps strategy, standards, and execution across all Sapiens projects for Life and P&C projects globally. The role builds and leads a global distributed DevOps organization spanning DevOps Architects and Engineers, and drives enterprise-wide standardization of SDLC/ALM automation, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code and container orchestration for project delivery. The role combines deep technical credibility in DevOps engineering with strategic leadership: toolchain governance, incident and production-support discipline, security and compliance in the delivery pipeline, and AI-augmented DevOps practices, all in close partnership with Engineering, Architecture, Security, and Product DevOps leadership across a multi-national organization.

Key Responsibilities

▪ Define and own the global DevOps strategy, standards, and multi-year roadmap across all Sapiens projects for Life and P&C projects globally.
▪ Build, lead, and scale a distributed, multi-national DevOps organization — DevOps Architects, Engineers, and Site Reliability specialists — supporting internal and external customers.
▪ Own the design, governance, and continuous improvement of automated SDLC/ALM solutions across the global project portfolio.
▪ Set enterprise-wide standards and governance for CI/CD pipeline design and implementation, including project delivery pipeline architecture, pipeline development, and equivalent modern CI/CD platforms.
▪ Own development infrastructure automation and management strategy, including Infrastructure-as-Code and Configuration-as-Code (IaC/CCA) practices across tools such as Terraform, Ansible, or SaltStack.
▪ Drive enterprise cloud infrastructure and architecture strategy, including container orchestration and management (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) across on-prem, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments.
▪ Own global incident and production-support governance, driving structured troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and preventive/corrective action across projects.
▪ Evaluate, select, and govern the adoption of new DevOps technologies and tools, ensuring reuse, standardization, and consistency across globally distributed teams.
▪ Define and reinforce enterprise DevSecOps standards, embedding security, compliance, and data-privacy requirements into pipelines and infrastructure automation.
▪ Define and govern enterprise-wide adoption of AI-augmented DevOps and SRE practices, including AI-assisted pipeline authoring, anomaly detection, and incident triage.
▪ Own budget, staffing, org design, and vendor/tooling decisions for the global DevOps function, optimizing cost, coverage, and the onshore/offshore delivery mix.
▪ Build organizational capability through hiring, mentoring, career development, and succession planning for DevOps Architects, Engineers, and emerging leaders.
▪ Own executive-level reporting on DevOps health, automation maturity, incident trends, and infrastructure risk across the global portfolio.
▪ Maintain comprehensive technical documentation standards and drive knowledge-sharing practices across a multi-national, multi-project DevOps organization.

Must Have Skills & Qualifications
Experience & Background

▪ 15+ years of experience in DevOps, infrastructure, or platform engineering, including 5+ years in a Director, Senior Manager, or Head of DevOps capacity leading global, multi-national teams.
▪ Proven track record owning DevOps strategy and standards across multiple concurrent projects, or business units at enterprise scale.
▪ Experience leading distributed, multi-national DevOps teams facing both internal and external customers.
▪ Demonstrated experience partnering with senior Engineering, Architecture, Security, and Product DevOps leadership on toolchain strategy, infrastructure investment, and technology adoption decisions.

Technical & Functional Skills

▪ Deep knowledge and understanding of SDLC/ALM architecture and processes, and proven experience governing them across multiple projects and teams.
▪ Strong expertise in Continuous Delivery/Deployment and Continuous Integration (CI/CD) solution design, development, and implementation at enterprise scale.
▪ Excellent knowledge of Jenkins internals and pipeline development with Groovy, or equivalent enterprise CI/CD platform expertise, with the ability to set standards across a global organization.
▪ Strong experience with high-level procedural/OO languages and scripting languages used in DevOps automation and tooling.
▪ Strong experience with Infrastructure-as-Code/Configuration-as-Code (IaC/CCA) solutions such as Terraform, Ansible, or SaltStack, and driving their adoption across teams.
▪ Strong experience with containers and container orchestration/management tools (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) at enterprise scale.
▪ Expertise in cloud infrastructure and architecture across major providers (preferably Microsoft Azure), including multi-cloud and hybrid strategies.
▪ Ability to set organization-wide standards for root-cause analysis and preventive action.

AI-Related Expectations

▪ Define and drive the enterprise strategy for AI-augmented DevOps and SRE practices, including AI-assisted pipeline authoring, infrastructure-as-code generation, anomaly detection, and incident triage.
▪ Establish governance, review discipline, and usage guardrails for AI-assisted outputs across the global DevOps organization.
▪ Champion AI literacy and capability-building across DevOps leadership and teams while ensuring human validation, security review, and correctness remain non-negotiable.
▪ Ensure AI adoption within DevOps follows approved privacy, security, and responsible-AI guidelines across all geographies.

Cloud & Infrastructure Awareness

▪ Deep, strategic understanding of cloud-hosted and SaaS delivery models, environment strategy, and release cadence, and their implications for infrastructure and pipeline design.
▪ Ability to guide global teams on multi-environment strategy (Dev, Test, UAT, Production) and configuration-driven, environment-specific automation.
▪ Awareness of how distributed, containerized, and elastic environments shape scalability, observability, and infrastructure risk at scale.

Communication & Leadership

▪ Excellent communication skills and a strong team-player orientation, with the ability to work effectively in a multi-national team facing internal and external customers.
▪ Strong people-leadership capability, including building high-performing global DevOps teams, mentoring senior engineers and architects, and developing future DevOps leaders.
▪ Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate DevOps strategy, risk, and progress clearly to senior leadership and stakeholders.
▪ Demonstrated change-management experience, with the ability to align diverse global stakeholders around shared DevOps standards and practices.

Personal Attributes

▪ Strong technical foundation and technological drive, with the credibility to engage hands-on when needed.
▪ Strong self-learner with the ability to adopt and succeed in a fast, dynamic, and evolving technology environment.
▪ Strategic thinker with strong ownership and accountability for global DevOps outcomes and infrastructure health.
▪ Collaborative leader who builds trust across geographies, functions, and levels of seniority.

Preferred / Good to Have

▪ Experience implementing and integrating new technologies across a large, distributed engineering organization.
▪ Cloud, Kubernetes, or DevOps-related certifications (e.g., AWS/Azure/GCP, CKA, or equivalent).
▪ Experience establishing or scaling global DevOps Centers of Excellence.
▪ Exposure to enterprise, regulated, or insurance-technology environments.
▪ Willingness to travel and support global stakeholders and teams across time zones as required.

jobAdDetails.title: VP, Development, Life Projects
jobAdDetails.description:
Description
 
The VP, Field Development, P&C Delivery owns the vision, strategy, and execution of engineering delivery across the complex, high-performance, enterprise-scale projects based on Sapiens' global Property & Casualty (P&C) product suite. The role spans the global organization of Architects, Engineering Managers, Technical Leads, and developers embedded in customer implementation, SaaS migration and SaaS support programs. The owner sets enterprise-wide delivery engineering standards and governance, and partners with delivery leadership to enhance engineering quality across the insurance platform. The role combines strategic leadership, organizational and budget ownership, process and AI-led automation modernization, of field development engineering to scale a high-performing, accountable global field development function. 

Key Responsibilities

jobAdDetails.title: Lead Business Value Delivery Architect/Solution Architect - ES
jobAdDetails.description:
Join Sapiens as our Lead Business Value Delivery Architect / Lead Solution Architect and play a pivotal role in taking client-facing insurance solutions from the sales cycle through delivery and into SaaS and AI platform migration, holding every engagement to a designed business outcome rather than an evolving list of requirements.

This is a role that sits between presales and delivery and stays engaged across both, spanning P&C, Life, and in future Reinsurance, with a particular focus on the non functional and operational requirements our industry consistently under-invests in. If you are deeply fluent in insurance product suites and platform roadmaps, comfortable holding both a head of claims and an engineer in the same conversation, and driven to keep clients and internal teams honest to the outcomes they signed up for - we'd love to hear from you.
jobAdDetails.requirements:
You'll own the professional and content thread of the solution end to end – across four connected areas of impact:
 
Value Definition – Presales solution design
 
  • Engage during the sales cycle, from general discovery through down select, to build product and industry context on the opportunity.
  • Frame the solution around the client's business outcomes, not a requirements checklist. Map what they are trying to achieve to what the platform actually delivers.
  • Establish a business outcome baseline with the client: what they will be able to do post go live that they cannot do today, and how both sides will measure it.
  • Own the definition of done, agreed jointly with the client.
  • Explicitly cover non functional and operational requirements: performance, scale, availability, security, integration, data migration, operability, and support, rather than leaving them to surface in build.
  • Feed into the implementation plan: the right order of implementation and the known dependencies, especially those on the client.
  • Where the platform does not meet the client's expected outcomes, own the resolution with Product and R&D. Either secure a commitment to build it into the core platform, with timelines aligned accordingly, or design it into the extension layer shipped with the core. The SA owns these conversations.
  • Act as the next layer of depth behind the presales and industry expert team. Presales surfaces the opportunity, the SA architects the solution.
  • Support the bid with clearly stated assumptions. The fixed price commercial construct itself is owned by Sales and the PD.
 
Delivery integrity
 
  • Move into rapid planning immediately after signing. Harden the solution against what the platform delivers, steering toward standard configuration over bespoke build.
  • Hand over a clear, documented solution design to the delivery team at the start of build, and safeguard the integrity of that design through delivery.
  • Hold all parties, internal teams and the client, accountable to the agreed business outcomes and how they will be achieved. This is outcome and professional accountability. The PM or PD holds delivery and the client to scope, timeline, and commitments.
  • Stay engaged through quarterly business reviews to catch outcome or value drift early.
  • Apply the definition of done. The project is complete only when the client is positioned to realise the value agreed at the outset, not simply when the system goes live.
 
Migration
 
  • For assigned clients, own migration outcomes through the analyse, dispose, bridge, and migrate framework, across the existing product portfolio and beyond.
  • Define, with each client, the specific value the migration unlocks and the KPIs that will confirm it. Migration is a value conversation, not only a technical one.
 
Tooling, AI, and continuous improvement
 
  • Serve as the first internal customer for AI in delivery, and own the tools and the standard for how they are used.
  • Set which source wins when inputs conflict: signed document over email, email over deck, deck over verbal.
  • Set what a human must verify in AI drafted work, rather than approve on sight.
  • Flag what the inputs do not say: tacit process, stakeholder disagreement, edge cases, not just what the AI summarised.
  • Work as part of the SA group to improve processes, outputs, and tools for quicker, better implementations, especially the SaaS migration factory, including a feedback loop from delivery back to discovery to recalibrate where discovery got the scope wrong.
 
What Success Looks Like:
 
  • Every signed programme has a documented, client agreed business outcome baseline, a joint definition of done, and go live success criteria.
  • Non functional and operational requirements are surfaced and designed in up front, not discovered in build.
  • Platform gaps are resolved deliberately, through a core platform commitment or an extension layer build, rather than emerging during delivery.
  • Delivery builds to the handed over design with minimal rework driven by scope or requirements ambiguity.
  • The SA group's processes, tools, and outputs measurably shorten implementations over time.
jobAdDetails.responsibilities:
You have a strong track record of designing or leading solution design in complex, enterprise-scale P&C insurance implementations, ideally across both presales and delivery. Extensive, hands-on P&C experience is essential for this role.
  • Deep P&C domain expertise across policy administration, underwriting, billing and claims, covering personal, commercial and/or specialty lines. Exposure to Reinsurance or the London Market is a plus.
  • Able to speak credibly to both a Head of Claims or Underwriting and an engineer.
  • Strong on non-functional and operational requirements, not only functional design: performance, scale, availability, security, integration and operability.
  • Proven ability to keep internal teams and clients aligned to agreed business outcomes. This accountability is central to the role, so it is a required skill, not just a welcome personality trait.
  • Experience with, or strong aptitude for, migrating P&C legacy or core systems to SaaS, including policy and claims data conversion.
  • Comfortable working in a function that is still being built. Process and tooling will be defined alongside the first deals.
  • Ideally, hands-on experience with cloud-native platforms and a proven track record at Born-in-the-Cloud (BIC) companies, bringing modern SaaS delivery practices to a global enterprise environment.
  • Skilled at using AI-driven tools and platforms to design, optimise and scale enterprise solution architectures.

jobAdDetails.title: Customer Delivery Executive
jobAdDetails.description:
Sapiens provides software for insurers worldwide, including property and casualty carriers. Our delivery teams help insurers move to modern cloud platforms and realise measurable business value.

The Customer Delivery Executive is the senior, customer-facing leader who makes sure our insurance customers reach real business value from their Sapiens investment, quickly and to a high standard. You partner with the customer's business and IT organisations as one team, own the business outcome the customer bought, and carry value realisation from Analysis and Design through to validated benefit.

You work with programme directors, project managers, solution architects and functional and technical experts across each engagement, and are based close to your customers, in their region.

Success looks like customers reaching usable business value quickly, value that is evidenced and reconciles with what was sold, reduced customisation against baseline, and AI agents showing a measurable gain against a pre-AI baseline.
jobAdDetails.requirements:
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 10+ years of insurance software implementation and deep knowledge of a core insurance platform and its roadmap (Sapiens core applications are a strong advantage).
  • Track record leading enterprise insurance software implementations and SaaS migrations, including legacy-to-SaaS moves, cloud-native practices and programmes across multiple regions.
  • Proven track record of building and scaling AI agent usage in customer-facing environments, such as AI-assisted coding, automated unit testing, documentation and release agents.
  • Experience building value cases, benefit-realisation plans or outcome-measurement frameworks that connect delivery milestones to business results.
  • PMP, PgMP, SAFe or an equivalent programme certification, and CSPO, SAFe POPM or an equivalent product-ownership credential.
  • Executive-level communication and influencing skills, with proven ability to manage executive escalations and multi-stakeholder conflicts without damaging the customer relationship.
  • Strong people leadership, including building high-performing teams and mentoring senior technical leaders, and first-hand understanding of delivery from the vendor side.
jobAdDetails.responsibilities:
• Own the customer outcome: partner with the customer's business and IT leaders, shape scope, priorities and approach, and turn the value case into measurable benefit milestones reviewed regularly with the customer.
  • Act as product owner: own backlog priority, define acceptance, hold the definition of done, and decide whether delivered work meets the customer promise.
  • Hold the end-to-end view of the final solution, including functionality, configuration, non-functional quality and evolving SaaS capabilities, with the final say on whether it delivers what the customer bought.
  • Shape the deal and carry it into delivery: join solution workshops with the solution architect, name every assumption, and test the delivery realism of scope, approach and effort before commitments are made.
  • Advise the customer and Sapiens on P&C market best practice, trends and regulation, and on what an insurance transformation demands beyond technology.
  • Keep Delivery, Product and R&D working together so gaps are minimised, decide which gaps become core product, and manage customisation expectations: standard first, never a fork of the core product.
  • Orchestrate AI agents in the delivery process, judge their output against the customer outcome, capture a baseline before they are switched on, and report the gain alongside schedule and quality.

jobAdDetails.title: Delivery CritSit Expert
jobAdDetails.description:
The CritSit Industry Expert is a senior member of the Critical Situations team. Your mission is to rapidly diagnose, stabilise and resolve complex customer crises on Sapiens insurance platforms, combining deep insurance expertise, technical curiosity, rigorous root cause analysis and unconventional problem solving.

You are an insurance expert with an engineering mindset who takes personal ownership of finding a viable solution. You work out what the product should be doing, what it is doing and what the business needs, then define the fix and drive it to resolution with Product Engineering, Delivery and CloudOps.

You bring deep expertise in one line of business: P&C, Life and Annuities, or Reinsurance. You stay composed when the customer is under pressure, explain complex problems simply, and insist on root cause rather than symptom relief.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to Critical Situations leadership, working alongside CritSit Managers, Engineering, Delivery and Support. Based at a regional hub, hybrid, with on-site visits at short notice.
jobAdDetails.requirements:
• 10+ years in insurance core systems, on the insurer, consultancy or vendor side, with deep expertise in one line: P&C, Life and Annuities, or Reinsurance.
  • Process depth in that line: product and rating, policy administration, billing and claims; for Reinsurance, treaty and facultative, cessions, bordereaux and accounting.
  • Strong product knowledge of core insurance platforms, with a working understanding of data models, integrations and data migration, enough to analyse problems and direct technical teams.
  • Strong business analysis skills, including requirements elicitation, process mapping, impact analysis and root cause analysis.
  • Practical experience applying AI to problem solving, such as analysing logs, documentation and past cases, with sound judgement to verify outputs and protect customer data.
  • A track record of resolving live problems in production or troubled implementations by defining the solution and working with technical teams to deliver it.
  • Ability to explain complex problems simply to executives and engineers alike.
  • Fluent English, hybrid working from a regional hub, and availability to be on site at short notice.
An advantage: experience of Sapiens platforms such as IDIT, CoreSuite and ReinsurancePro, cloud and SaaS experience, an underwriting or actuarial background, and data analysis skills or a business analysis certification.
jobAdDetails.responsibilities:
• Join critical situations early and diagnose them rapidly, working out how the product, configuration, data and the customer's business process interact.
  • Analyse business requirements, product behaviour, logs and data extracts, and test hypotheses until the cause is clear.
  • Use approved AI tools to speed up analysis of logs, documentation and past cases, and verify every output before relying on it or sharing it with a customer.
  • Define a working fix or safe workaround that stabilises the customer's live operation, and agree it with Engineering and Delivery.
  • Translate business impact into clear requirements, expected behaviour and acceptance criteria, and stay accountable until the customer confirms resolution.
  • Design and assess unconventional solutions, such as process changes or configuration alternatives, weighing business and product risk before recommending them.
  • Find and document the root cause of every escalation, verify the fix holds, and prevent repeats: no stabilised escalation recurs within 90 days.
  • Turn each case into reusable diagnostics and fixes, and add them to the playbook every quarter.
  • Explain complex problems and options simply to customer executives, delivery leads and engineers, and give the CritSit Manager accurate findings and next steps.
  • Work with Support, Delivery, Engineering and Product to hand over fixes, share product know-how, and give clear feedback on gaps, defects and enhancement needs.
  • Keep current with Sapiens platform releases and the customer's configuration, so diagnosis starts from knowledge, not guesswork.

jobAdDetails.title: Regional Delivery CritSit Leader
jobAdDetails.description:
The Regional Leader, Critical Situations owns how Sapiens resolves high-severity customer escalations across their region, and works to stop them recurring by spotting risk trends early. You lead a team of CritSit Managers, represent the function with customer C-level executives and the Sapiens senior leadership team, and bring Delivery, Customer Success, Sales, Engineering and Product together when customer trust is most exposed.

The role carries commercial as well as operational accountability: you quantify the financial impact of critical situations and programme delays, and agree the commercial actions that follow. You work to the global CritSit framework and adapt it to your region's needs and regulatory context.

This is a Senior Manager or Director level role in Delivery Program Management, reporting to the Senior Vice President (SVP). Based at a regional hub, hybrid, with regular customer travel.
jobAdDetails.requirements:
• 12+ years in enterprise software delivery or customer success, including 5+ years leading teams through critical situations or programme recovery.
  • Project and risk management experience across a regional portfolio, including reading monthly business reviews and account reviews for trends that precede an escalation.
  • Commercial responsibility and sound judgement: moving projects from time and expenses to fixed pricing, and quantifying the financial impact of a CritSit or programme delay.
  • Proven people leadership, including leading and developing managers across a multi-team or multi-country organisation.
  • Executive presence with customer C-level executives and senior leadership.
  • Insurance industry and core-systems knowledge across the region's lines of business.
  • Technical fluency across cloud infrastructure, APIs and integrations, and working knowledge of incident management tools such as Jira, ServiceNow and Salesforce.
  • Fluent English, availability for regular customer travel, and a bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
An advantage: experience of insurance or financial SaaS platforms, P&L responsibility, a further regional language, and ITIL or PMP certification.
jobAdDetails.responsibilities:
• Set the regional vision, priorities and roadmap for CritSit management, aligned with the global strategy.
  • Build, coach and develop a team of CritSit Managers, and apply the global severity definitions and escalation paths.
  • Act as executive point of accountability for the region's most critical, highest-revenue or reputationally sensitive escalations, engaging customer C-level executives directly.
  • Brief the SVP and senior leadership promptly and candidly, and escalate early when a case needs global attention.
  • Own project and risk management across the regional portfolio, with every critical situation under a named owner and a recovery plan.
  • Spot trends in monthly business and account reviews and act on them before customers do.
  • Quantify the financial impact of CritSits and programme delays, and work with Sales to move projects from time and expenses to fixed pricing where it protects the customer and Sapiens.
  • Work with Engineering, CloudOps and DevOps, Product, InfoSec, Sales, Customer Success, Legal and Communications to prioritise fixes, remove blockers and handle regulatory or public implications.
  • Hold teams to account for corrective and preventive actions with clear owners and deadlines.
  • Run the regional root-cause and post-incident review programme, and report regional KPIs: time to engage, mitigate and resolve, repeat incidents, SLA adherence, CritSit ageing and revenue protected.
  • Contribute to the global CritSit playbook and tooling, and run readiness programmes for regional teams.

jobAdDetails.title: Delivery CritSit Manager
jobAdDetails.description:
The Manager, Critical Situations owns the resolution of high-severity customer situations (CritSits) on Sapiens delivery engagements: major defects, stalled implementations, data issues and at-risk programmes. You are the single point of accountability from the moment a CritSit is declared to the moment it is closed, leading a cross-functional team without formal line authority.

You are the calmest voice in a tense room: accountable, candid, empathetic, decisive and organised.
This is an individual contributor role in Delivery Success, reporting to the Delivery Success CritSit Regional Leader. Based at a regional hub, hybrid, with on-site visits at short notice and an after-hours on-call rotation.
jobAdDetails.requirements:
• 7+ years in customer-facing technology, incident or escalation roles, including first-hand experience as an Incident Commander or crisis lead.
  • Programme management expertise, including recovering troubled programmes through planning, risk management, governance and change control.
  • Track record of owning high-impact outages and severe escalations end to end, running the war room and mobilising teams with no reporting line.
  • Working knowledge of insurance or financial-services core systems, enough to judge business impact.
  • Clear, accurate communication with customers and senior leaders, setting expectations early.
  • Practical experience using AI tools to improve incident management.
  • Fluent English, availability for after-hours on-call, and willingness to travel to customer sites at short notice.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
An advantage: ITIL major-incident practice, a further European language, and PMP, PRINCE2 or similar certification.
jobAdDetails.responsibilities:
• Own high-impact outages and severe escalations from first report to close-out, triaging against agreed severity criteria.
  • Run the war room, including bridge calls and a dedicated Slack or Teams channel, setting priorities, owners and action plans.
  • Agree a recovery plan within days of declaration, with milestones, dependencies and exit criteria, and manage risks, issues and re-baselined timelines.
  • Agree resourcing with Delivery leadership and hold programme governance until the customer is back on track.
  • Give customers and leadership clear, regular updates, translating technical detail into business impact and next steps.
  • Escalate to business leadership when decisions exceed agreed limits.
  • Mobilise Engineering, CloudOps and DevOps, Support and Product, and keep Sales, Customer Success and Account Management aligned.
  • Drive root-cause analysis, the customer-facing report and the post-mortem, and make sure corrective and preventive actions are delivered.
  • Spot patterns across engagements and releases, and report CritSit metrics: time to engage, mitigate and resolve, repeat incidents, ageing, and milestone adherence.

jobAdDetails.title: AI Forward Deployed Engineer (AI-FDE)
jobAdDetails.description:
Sapiens has something truly unique. Over 40 years, we’ve built deep insurance expertise that no-one else can replicate. Combined with the power of SapiensAIP that knowledge gives us an extraordinary opportunity to transform how insurance works, and to help build the autonomous insurer of tomorrow.
This is where Advance the Possible comes in. It isn’t a programme or a new strategy. It’s our DNA. It’s about how we think, work and challenge ourselves every day. It means moving with greater urgency, questioning old ways of working and creating better outcomes for our customers.  Go to https://sapiens.com to find out more. 

Location: Singapore

Come and join us now! 

PURPOSE
Turn ambiguous customer problems into production AI capability, fast, as the technical half of the Value FDE and AI-FDE pair.

Find the problem worth solving, turn it into a live buildable backlog, redesign the process around AI and make sure the value lands

jobAdDetails.title: Lead Business Value Delivery Architect/Solution Architect - SG
jobAdDetails.description:
Join Sapiens as our Lead Business Value Delivery Architect / Lead Solution Architect and play a pivotal role in taking client-facing insurance solutions from the sales cycle through delivery and into SaaS and AI platform migration, holding every engagement to a designed business outcome rather than an evolving list of requirements.

This is a role that sits between presales and delivery and stays engaged across both, spanning P&C, Life, and in future Reinsurance, with a particular focus on the non functional and operational requirements our industry consistently under-invests in. If you are deeply fluent in insurance product suites and platform roadmaps, comfortable holding both a head of claims and an engineer in the same conversation, and driven to keep clients and internal teams honest to the outcomes they signed up for - we'd love to hear from you.

What Success Looks Like:
 
  • Every signed programme has a documented, client agreed business outcome baseline, a joint definition of done, and go live success criteria.
  • Non functional and operational requirements are surfaced and designed in up front, not discovered in build.
  • Platform gaps are resolved deliberately, through a core platform commitment or an extension layer build, rather than emerging during delivery.
  • Delivery builds to the handed over design with minimal rework driven by scope or requirements ambiguity.
  • The SA group's processes, tools, and outputs measurably shorten implementations over time.
jobAdDetails.requirements:
You'll own the professional and content thread of the solution end to end – across four connected areas of impact:
 
  1. Value Definition – Presales solution design
 
  • Engage during the sales cycle, from general discovery through down select, to build product and industry context on the opportunity.
  • Frame the solution around the client's business outcomes, not a requirements checklist. Map what they are trying to achieve to what the platform actually delivers.
  • Establish a business outcome baseline with the client: what they will be able to do post go live that they cannot do today, and how both sides will measure it.
  • Own the definition of done, agreed jointly with the client.
  • Explicitly cover non functional and operational requirements: performance, scale, availability, security, integration, data migration, operability, and support, rather than leaving them to surface in build.
  • Feed into the implementation plan: the right order of implementation and the known dependencies, especially those on the client.
  • Where the platform does not meet the client's expected outcomes, own the resolution with Product and R&D. Either secure a commitment to build it into the core platform, with timelines aligned accordingly, or design it into the extension layer shipped with the core. The SA owns these conversations.
  • Act as the next layer of depth behind the presales and industry expert team. Presales surfaces the opportunity, the SA architects the solution.
  • Support the bid with clearly stated assumptions. The fixed price commercial construct itself is owned by Sales and the PD.
 
  1. Delivery integrity
 
  • Move into rapid planning immediately after signing. Harden the solution against what the platform delivers, steering toward standard configuration over bespoke build.
  • Hand over a clear, documented solution design to the delivery team at the start of build, and safeguard the integrity of that design through delivery.
  • Hold all parties, internal teams and the client, accountable to the agreed business outcomes and how they will be achieved. This is outcome and professional accountability. The PM or PD holds delivery and the client to scope, timeline, and commitments.
  • Stay engaged through quarterly business reviews to catch outcome or value drift early.
  • Apply the definition of done. The project is complete only when the client is positioned to realise the value agreed at the outset, not simply when the system goes live.
 
  1. Migration
 
  • For assigned clients, own migration outcomes through the analyse, dispose, bridge, and migrate framework, across the existing product portfolio and beyond.
  • Define, with each client, the specific value the migration unlocks and the KPIs that will confirm it. Migration is a value conversation, not only a technical one.
 
  1. Tooling, AI, and continuous improvement
 
  • Serve as the first internal customer for AI in delivery, and own the tools and the standard for how they are used.
  • Set which source wins when inputs conflict: signed document over email, email over deck, deck over verbal.
  • Set what a human must verify in AI drafted work, rather than approve on sight.
  • Flag what the inputs do not say: tacit process, stakeholder disagreement, edge cases, not just what the AI summarised.
  • Work as part of the SA group to improve processes, outputs, and tools for quicker, better implementations, especially the SaaS migration factory, including a feedback loop from delivery back to discovery to recalibrate where discovery got the scope wrong.
jobAdDetails.responsibilities:
• You have a track record designing or leading solution design in complex, enterprise insurance implementations, ideally spanning both presales and delivery.
  • Ability to speak credibly to both a head of claims and an engineer, across P&C, Life, and Reinsurance.
  • Strong on non functional and operational requirements: performance, scale, availability, security, integration, operability, not only functional design.
  • Demonstrated ability to hold the professional and outcome vector, keeping internal teams and clients aligned to agreed business outcomes. Given that this accountability is a core responsibility of the role, it is a required skill, not simply a welcome personality trait.
  • Experience with, or strong aptitude for, legacy to SaaS or core platform migration work.
  • Comfortable operating in a function that is still being built. Process and tooling will be defined in parallel with the first deals.
  • You ideally have hands-on experience with cloud-native platforms and a proven track record working at Born-in-the-Cloud (BIC) companies, bringing modern SaaS delivery practices to a global enterprise environment.
  • Proficient in leveraging AI-driven tools and platforms to design, optimize, and scale enterprise solution architectures.

Interested? We'd love to hear from you. Our TA partner evija.briska@sapiens.com is your contact for any questions. We kindly ask that you apply via our website or LinkedIn.

jobAdDetails.title: Customer Delivery Executive
jobAdDetails.description:
Sapiens provides software for insurers worldwide, including property and casualty carriers. Our delivery teams help insurers move to modern cloud platforms and realise measurable business value.

The Customer Delivery Executive is the senior, customer-facing leader who makes sure our insurance customers reach real business value from their Sapiens investment, quickly and to a high standard. You partner with the customer's business and IT organisations as one team, own the business outcome the customer bought, and carry value realisation from Analysis and Design through to validated benefit.

You work with programme directors, project managers, solution architects and functional and technical experts across each engagement, and are based close to your customers, in their region.

Success looks like customers reaching usable business value quickly, value that is evidenced and reconciles with what was sold, reduced customisation against baseline, and AI agents showing a measurable gain against a pre-AI baseline.
jobAdDetails.requirements:
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field.
  • 10+ years of insurance software implementation and deep knowledge of a core insurance platform and its roadmap (Sapiens core applications are a strong advantage).
  • Track record leading enterprise insurance software implementations and SaaS migrations, including legacy-to-SaaS moves, cloud-native practices and programmes across multiple regions.
  • Proven track record of building and scaling AI agent usage in customer-facing environments, such as AI-assisted coding, automated unit testing, documentation and release agents.
  • Experience building value cases, benefit-realisation plans or outcome-measurement frameworks that connect delivery milestones to business results.
  • PMP, PgMP, SAFe or an equivalent programme certification, and CSPO, SAFe POPM or an equivalent product-ownership credential.
  • Executive-level communication and influencing skills, with proven ability to manage executive escalations and multi-stakeholder conflicts without damaging the customer relationship.
  • Strong people leadership, including building high-performing teams and mentoring senior technical leaders, and first-hand understanding of delivery from the vendor side.
jobAdDetails.responsibilities:
• Own the customer outcome: partner with the customer's business and IT leaders, shape scope, priorities and approach, and turn the value case into measurable benefit milestones reviewed regularly with the customer.
  • Act as product owner: own backlog priority, define acceptance, hold the definition of done, and decide whether delivered work meets the customer promise.
  • Hold the end-to-end view of the final solution, including functionality, configuration, non-functional quality and evolving SaaS capabilities, with the final say on whether it delivers what the customer bought.
  • Shape the deal and carry it into delivery: join solution workshops with the solution architect, name every assumption, and test the delivery realism of scope, approach and effort before commitments are made.
  • Advise the customer and Sapiens on P&C market best practice, trends and regulation, and on what an insurance transformation demands beyond technology.
  • Keep Delivery, Product and R&D working together so gaps are minimised, decide which gaps become core product, and manage customisation expectations: standard first, never a fork of the core product.
  • Orchestrate AI agents in the delivery process, judge their output against the customer outcome, capture a baseline before they are switched on, and report the gain alongside schedule and quality.

More about the role and it’s purpose …
 
You will own the execution and delivery integrity of Sapiens customer Programmes. This role sits within the Delivery Success team and is the primary accountable leader for Programme governance, milestone management, and value delivery inside a customer engagement.
 
You will be a senior delivery leader with deep insurance and financial services fluency, commercial discipline, and the judgement to run complex, multi-workstream Programmes at pace. You will run an AI-native delivery model with a progressively automated execution layer, freeing the role for discernment, governance, and the customer relationship. jobAdDetails.requirements:

  • Deep insurance domain knowledge is preferred: Life & Pension, Property & Casualty, or equivalent specialty lines. Experience in fintech or broader financial services technology will also be considered.  
  • Familiarity with Policy Administration Systems and the insurance technology landscape - or comparable core platforms in financial services - is strongly preferred.

  • Experience leading global cross-functional teams including SI partners, offshore delivery resources, and customer-side teams in a matrixed environment.
  • AI transformation experience:  practical comfort directing AI tools across Programme management functions, evaluating AI-generated outputs, and operating an AI-native delivery model.
  • Programme financial management:  budget ownership, forecasting, cost-to-serve awareness, and milestone-based billing alignment.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. Comfortable running steering committees, presenting to senior customer leadership, and managing difficult conversations with clarity.

jobAdDetails.responsibilities:
01 - Programme Delivery & Commercial Outcomes
 
  • End-to-end delivery ownership: Leads the full Programme lifecycle from initiation through planning, execution, and closure. Accountable for delivery on time, within scope, and within budget across all workstreams – including platform implementation, integration, data migration, and business change.
  • Time to Value: Owns the pace at which the customer realises measurable outcomes. Sets the time-to-value baseline at programme initiation, tracks it at every milestone, and uses delivery decisions to shorten it. Accountable for committed implementation timelines - and for turning outperformance into a commercial conversation.
  • AI-led SaaS implementation velocity:  Moves Programmes toward faster implementation cycles consistent with Sapiens’ AI-led SaaS delivery model. Understands the configuration-over-customisation discipline and applies it to keep Programmes on the standard implementation trajectory that maximises customer time-to-value.
  • Commercial Outcomes – In partnership with Customer Success, owns NRR contribution of the customer portfolio. Knows the expansion levers, drives them, and reports against them.
  • Growth - Identifies upsell and cross-sell potential during delivery and converts insight into pipeline opportunities.
  • AI-native execution model: Operates a delivery model in which AI handles the execution layer: status tracking, risk summarisation, documentation, meeting outputs, and reporting cadences. Directs AI tools, evaluates their output, and uses them to accelerate Programme pace and free team capacity for judgement-intensive work.
 
02 - Milestone Management & Exit Criteria
 
  • Milestone ownership: Defines, manages, and tracks Programme milestones with precision. Each milestone has a clear definition of done, an agreed exit criteria, and formal customer acceptance before the Programme advances. This is the primary mechanism for preventing red projects.
  • Exit criteria discipline: Works with the customer to agree exit criteria at the start of each phase – not at the end. Any customer request that falls outside accepted exit criteria is a natural change order, not a negotiation. The PDE holds this boundary with clarity and without conflict.
  • Milestone-based billing alignment:  Ensures that delivery milestones align with commercial billing triggers. Milestone acceptance by the customer is both a delivery gate and a commercial event. The PDE manages both dimensions in coordination with the Customer Success team.
  • Risk and dependency management:  Maintains a live Programme risk register. Identifies, assesses, and mitigates risks before they become issues. Manages interdependencies across workstreams, vendors, and internal Sapiens teams. Surfaces conflicts and trade-offs early and drives resolution with pace.
 
03 – Insurance & Financial Services Industry Fluency
 
  • Domain depth: Builds and maintains a deep understanding of the customer's business - P&L drivers, operating model, competitive pressures, and regulatory environment. Speaks insurance fluently, or has fluency in financial services technology.
  • Insurance Ontology and AutonomousInsurer thesis: Carries the Sapiens point of view into every engagement - articulating why a shared data model across the insurance value chain creates structural advantage, and what the AI-native insurance operating model looks like. Uses both to elevate the conversation beyond current project scope. 
 
04 - Proactive Customer Relationship & Escalation Management
 
  • Customer relationship ownership at the Programme level: Holds the customer relationship at the C-suite level on substance and trust. Is the person the customer calls when something genuinely matters.
  • Proactive escalation management: Acts ahead of the problem, not in response to it. Reads signals early customer frustration, delivery drift, scope ambiguity – and raises the difficult conversation before it becomes a crisis. Foresees escalations and prevents them through structured, proactive management.
  • Partners closely with the account's Customer Success Manager — the PDE owns delivery execution, CS owns the commercial relationship and expansion. Together they own the Customer Value Journey, with a clean, documented handoff. Customer health is a shared metric. 
 
05 - Resource Orchestration & Team Leadership
 
  • Cross-functional team orchestration:  Manages delivery across blended teams: Sapiens employees, offshore delivery resources, SI partners, and customer-side teams. Ensures alignment, accountability, and pace across all.
  • Team leadership and development:  Builds capability with intention, treating team development as a commercial lever rather than an HR task. Leads the full talent lifecycle with candour and integrity.
  • Sapiens ambassadorship: Carries the Sapiens point of view into customer environments. Knows the Insurance Ontology argument, the AutonomousInsurer thesis, and the AI moat – and can hold them in a room.
  • Leads the Programme's PM team, setting standards and driving accountability. As the account's delivery standard-setter, the PDE defines the level the team performs to.

jobAdDetails.title: Lead Business Value Delivery Architect/Solution Architect - UK
jobAdDetails.description:
Join Sapiens as our Lead Business Value Delivery Architect / Lead Solution Architect and play a pivotal role in taking client-facing insurance solutions from the sales cycle through delivery and into SaaS and AI platform migration, holding every engagement to a designed business outcome rather than an evolving list of requirements.

This is a role that sits between presales and delivery and stays engaged across both, spanning P&C, Life, and in future Reinsurance, with a particular focus on the non functional and operational requirements our industry consistently under-invests in. If you are deeply fluent in insurance product suites and platform roadmaps, comfortable holding both a head of claims and an engineer in the same conversation, and driven to keep clients and internal teams honest to the outcomes they signed up for - we'd love to hear from you.

What Success Looks Like:
 
  • Every signed programme has a documented, client agreed business outcome baseline, a joint definition of done, and go live success criteria.
  • Non functional and operational requirements are surfaced and designed in up front, not discovered in build.
  • Platform gaps are resolved deliberately, through a core platform commitment or an extension layer build, rather than emerging during delivery.
  • Delivery builds to the handed over design with minimal rework driven by scope or requirements ambiguity.
  • The SA group's processes, tools, and outputs measurably shorten implementations over time.
jobAdDetails.requirements:
You'll own the professional and content thread of the solution end to end – across four connected areas of impact:
 
Value Definition – Presales solution design
 
  • Engage during the sales cycle, from general discovery through down select, to build product and industry context on the opportunity.
  • Frame the solution around the client's business outcomes, not a requirements checklist. Map what they are trying to achieve to what the platform actually delivers.
  • Establish a business outcome baseline with the client: what they will be able to do post go live that they cannot do today, and how both sides will measure it.
  • Own the definition of done, agreed jointly with the client.
  • Explicitly cover non functional and operational requirements: performance, scale, availability, security, integration, data migration, operability, and support, rather than leaving them to surface in build.
  • Feed into the implementation plan: the right order of implementation and the known dependencies, especially those on the client.
  • Where the platform does not meet the client's expected outcomes, own the resolution with Product and R&D. Either secure a commitment to build it into the core platform, with timelines aligned accordingly, or design it into the extension layer shipped with the core. The SA owns these conversations.
  • Act as the next layer of depth behind the presales and industry expert team. Presales surfaces the opportunity, the SA architects the solution.
  • Support the bid with clearly stated assumptions. The fixed price commercial construct itself is owned by Sales and the PD.
 
Delivery integrity
 
  • Move into rapid planning immediately after signing. Harden the solution against what the platform delivers, steering toward standard configuration over bespoke build.
  • Hand over a clear, documented solution design to the delivery team at the start of build, and safeguard the integrity of that design through delivery.
  • Hold all parties, internal teams and the client, accountable to the agreed business outcomes and how they will be achieved. This is outcome and professional accountability. The PM or PD holds delivery and the client to scope, timeline, and commitments.
  • Stay engaged through quarterly business reviews to catch outcome or value drift early.
  • Apply the definition of done. The project is complete only when the client is positioned to realise the value agreed at the outset, not simply when the system goes live.
 
Migration

jobAdDetails.title: Critical Situations Expert
jobAdDetails.description:
The CritSit Industry Expert is a member of the CritSit team. The mission is to rapidly diagnose, stabilize, and resolve complex customer crises by combining deep insurance expertise, technical curiosity, rigorous root cause analysis, and unconventional problem solving.

This is a highly capable insurance expert who operates with an engineering mindset and takes personal ownership of discovering a viable solution. The role is built on product knowledge and business analysis: the Industry Expert works out what the product should be doing, what it is doing, and what the business needs, then defines the solution and drives it to resolution with Product Engineering, Delivery and CloudOps.
jobAdDetails.requirements:
• 10 or more years in insurance core systems, on the insurer, consultancy, or vendor side, with deep expertise in one line: P&C, Life and Annuities, or Reinsurance.
  • Process depth in that line: product and rating, policy administration, billing, and claims; for Reinsurance, treaty and facultative, cessions, bordereaux, and accounting.
  • Strong product knowledge of core insurance platforms, with a working understanding of data models, integrations, and data migration, enough to analyze problems and direct technical teams.
  • Strong business analysis skills, including requirements elicitation, process mapping, impact analysis, and root cause analysis.
  • Practical experience of applying AI to problem solving, such as analyzing logs, documentation, and past cases, with sound judgement to verify outputs and protect customer data.
  • A track record of resolving live problems in production or in troubled implementations by defining the solution and working with technical teams to deliver it.
  • The ability to explain complex problems simply to executives and engineers alike.
  • Fluent English.
  • Availability to work from a regional hub on a hybrid basis, and to be on site at short notice.

The following are an advantage:
  • Experience of Sapiens platforms, such as IDIT, CoreSuite, and ReinsurancePro.
  • Cloud and SaaS experience.
  • An underwriting or actuarial background.
Technical skills for data analysis, or a business analysis certification
jobAdDetails.responsibilities:
Diagnose and Define
  • Join critical situations early and diagnose the problem rapidly, working out how the product, configuration, data, and the customer’s business process interact.
  • Analyse business requirements, product behaviour, logs, and data extracts supplied by the technical teams, and test hypotheses until the cause is clear.
  • Use approved AI tools to speed up analysis of logs, documentation, and past cases, and verify every output before relying on it or sharing it with a customer.
  • Define a working fix or safe workaround that stabilizes the customer’s live operation, and agree it with Engineering and Delivery for implementation.

Solution Definition and Ownership
  • Translate business impact into clear requirements, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria for the fix.
  • Work with Engineering, Delivery, and CloudOps to implement and verify fixes, and stay accountable until the customer confirms resolution.
  • Design and assess unconventional solutions, such as process changes or configuration alternatives, when standard approaches have failed, and weigh their business and product risk before recommending them.

Root Cause and Prevention
  • Find and document the root cause of every escalation, and verify that the fix holds.
  • Prevent repeats: no stabilized escalation recurs within 90 days.
  • Turn each case into reusable diagnostics and fixes, and add them to the playbook every quarter.

Communication and Collaboration
  • Explain complex problems and options simply to customer executives, delivery leads, and engineers.
  • Supply accurate technical findings and next steps to the CritSit Manager, who runs the war room and customer updates.
  • Work with Support, Delivery, Engineering, and Product to hand over fixes and share product know-how.

Product and Domain Expertise
  • Apply deep expertise in one line of business, and in the Sapiens products, to judge business impact and define correct behavior.
  • Keep current with Sapiens platform releases and the customer’s configuration, so that diagnosis starts from knowledge, not guesswork.
  • Give Product management clear feedback on gaps, defects, and enhancement needs that critical situations reveal.
